Aging at 450 °C for three hours produced very fine precipitates, less than 15 nm in size. The high hardness of the 450 °C-3h aged sample (Figure 1b) is attributed to the formation of these homogeneous ly distributed, fine and coherent precipitates.
Aging at 550 °C for three hours resulted in the formation of larger precipitates (~15–20 nm) with lower density when compared to the 450 °C-3h condition.
H-phase precipitates, ~40–70 nm in size, were obser ved after aging at 650 °C for three hours (Figure 2k).
